utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: For the duration of your evidence, you will be known as Witness B-083.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the exhibits for this witness be given a collective number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 507.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown tab 1 of Exhibit 507, an exhibit to be kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just yes or no: Does this piece of paper contain your curriculum vitae?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witness B-083, paragraph 1 of the summary, did you work for a period of time in the Serbian Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-083
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 5: Were the succession of ministers at the Ministry of Defence respectively Admiral Jokic followed by General Simovic, followed by General Negovanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 7: When Simovic became minister, was he joined by Major-General Kuzmanovic, assistant to the minister for military issues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 19: Are you aware of the existence of something called the coordination group which was associated with General Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May we look now, please, at Exhibits 427, tabs 37 and 38. Tab 37 first.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If I can remind the Chamber through the witness of what is on the document. Sorry, it's on Sanction. Yes. Thank you very much. Can we see the English -- yes. Do Your Honours have an English version of this document in order to refresh your memories as to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- what it contains? And for those who would not be able to read the B/C/S, it's a document of the 1st of November, 1991 from the Republic of Serbia's Ministry of Defence, seeking that, on the agenda of the government session, there should be placed the report on assisting Serbian areas in Croatia, and the document says, "Given the importance and level of confidentiality, the items should be discussed at a government session closed to the public." Signed by Major-General Kuzmanovic, apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witness B-083, is that a signature you recognise? If so, whose is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-083
utterances.text: It is the signature of Major-General Branislav Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-083
utterances.text: I consider it to be authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Exhibit 427, tab 38. Again, I trust that the Chamber has the original in English, being a document from the Republic of Serbia's National Defence to the -- the Republic of Serbia's Ministry of Defence, dated the 1st of November, for the government of the Republic of Serbia, being a report on providing assistance to Serbian districts in Croatia. And as the Chamber may recall, being a document which on its first English translation side says at the beginning of the second paragraph, "Having considered top priorities several times and having reduced them to the most essential needs of the Serbs in Croatia" -- it goes on on the second page to set out the financial assistance to be provided for November and December 1991 in the sum of 1 billion 205 million dinars, which equates to, I think, 92.000-odd Deutschmarks, according to evidence we've already had -- 92 million-odd Deutschmarks. Sorry. The figures are sometimes confused. The only thing we want from you, please, Witness B-083 is this: Do you see a signature at the foot of the document? If so, do you recognise it and whose is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-083
utterances.text: There's no signature here -- yes. Yes, there is. I'm sorry. Branislav Kuzmanovic, Major-General.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think you're looking at the wrong part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can he have, please, tab 38. And can he have it at the second sheet in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-083
utterances.text: I do, but this is not Tomislav Simovic but Branislav Kuzmanovic who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We may return to that issue a little later tomorrow. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, when you get to a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next paragraph, 33: In general terms, please, Witness B-083, for payments out from Ministry of Defence funds, in addition to the obvious authority of the minister, who else would have authority to order the payment out of funds from the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-083
utterances.text: In addition to the Minister of Defence, the signature was deposited of the deputy minister and other persons who he considered could represent him in those transactions. And I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If Your Honour is looking for a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness B-083, we're going to adjourn. I'm sorry you haven't been able to give evidence for longer, but we'll hear the rest of your evidence tomorrow. Could you remember during the adjournment not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. We'll ask you to be back at 9.00 tomorrow. Before you can go though, the blinds have got to be brought down. And I'm going to deal with some administrative matters first. This has nothing to do with you. It's purely administrative, so I'm going to deal with that -- No, not for the moment. I'm going to give these -- I'm going to give some rulings about evidence which have nothing to do with you. The first ruling deals with the statements of the following witnesses: B-1750, 1488, 1524, 1460, 1516, 1097, 1704, 1010, 1502. These statements all deal with events associated with the takeover of Bijeljina, Zvornik, and Bratunac municipalities. Much evidence has already been given about those events. The statement of the witnesses -- the statements of the witnesses are cumulative, and they will be admitted under Rule 92 bis (A). The Prosecution concedes that these witnesses should attend for cross-examination except for two, B-1010 and B-1516. The accused objects to any admission of statements and a fortiori would object to any statement being admitted without cross-examination. The amici make no objection in relation to B-1516, pointing out that the evidence is purely cumulative, identifying Repic as the perpetrator of the crimes committed against detainees at Celopek. He was identified as the perpetrator before and this was not challenged. For these reasons, the Trial Chamber will admit the statement without cross-examination. In relation to B-1010, the amici point out that the statement involves a significant allegation, as it does. However, the Prosecution point out that the evidence is purely cumulative of that given by Witness B-1701, who was extensively cross-examined as to the presence of the JNA. Furthermore, they will be calling another witness to give evidence about the takeover of Bratunac who can be cross-examined. It is also to be noted that the witness identifies the soldiers as local Serbs, rather than the regular JNA. In these circumstances, there is no significant live issue for the witness to be cross-examined about; therefore, these nine statements will be admitted under Rule 92 bis, the statements of witnesses B-1516 and 1010 will be admitted without cross-examination, the remainder must attend for cross-examination. There are two further short rulings which it would be convenient to deal with now. Apologies to the interpreters for the absence of a text, but as I say, they're short. First, concerning Witness B-1241, to whom a Prosecution motion of the 7th of July relates, requesting the admission of a transcript and a written statement of the witness under Rule 92 bis. We have also the amici observations and the Prosecution reply. We have come to the conclusion that this witness's evidence should be heard live because of the overriding public interest in doing so, involving as it does significant allegations in the Bosnia indictment, the involvement of persons such as Mladic in the joint criminal enterprise and the cooperation between Serbia and the VRS. Finally, the motion concerning a statement of Ana Bicani. I may have the name wrong -- Bicanic, I should say. We have considered that motion, which is to substitute her evidence for that of another witness and admit the evidence under Rule 92 bis with cross-examination. We've received no submissions from the amici. The evidence is cumulative regarding the attack upon Saborsko. Leave to substitute will be given. The statement will be admitted under Rule 92 bis, the witness to attend for cross-examination. We will adjourn now until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
